question.problem: Use the difference of squares method to solve the equation $49{j}^{2}-64=0.$
question.worked_solution:
Using the difference of squares formula, we factor the left-hand side of our quadratic equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}49{j}^{2}-64 & =0 \\ (7j)^{2}-{8}^{2} & =0 \\ (7j-8)(7j+8) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the zero product rule, we have

$$
7j-8=0\,\text{or}\,7j+8=0.
$$

Then, we solve each equation separately:

$$
\begin{aligned}7j-8 & =0 & \, & \, & 7j+8 & =0 \\ 7j & =8 & \, & \, & 7j & =-8 \\ j & =\frac{8}{7} & \, & \, & j & =-\frac{8}{7}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solutions are $j=-\frac{8}{7},\frac{8}{7}.$ We can write this even more concisely as $j=\pm \frac{8}{7}.$
